BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Taken together, the changes would greatly reduce the Seller's real exposure:

- every claim, including title and fraud, falls under one low cap;
- a high basket and short claims period apply;
- disclosure of the entire data room is deemed;
- a blanket buyer-knowledge bar applies.

Several known problems (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) would be left unresolved at Completion. We should reject the package's framing and send a full mark-up.

---

## 1. The "settled" and "[STANDARD]" framing

The covering note says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL," and that [STANDARD] clauses "need no further scrutiny." **We should not accept this. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.**

- **We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost** approving any fallback, including the 20% cap or the 18-month period, for this draft. Under our playbook, an oral or reported "principal-level" agreement does not unlock a fallback. If the Seller says Amelia agreed something, confirm it with her directly. Do not rely on the Seller's description.
- The "[STANDARD]" labels are the Seller's own. Many of the most buyer-adverse terms carry that label: the fraud override, the buyer-knowledge bar, consent-on-delivery and the post-completion Riverlark release.
- The "market context" (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months) is advocacy, not agreed terms. It does not override our mandate.
- The reviewer note says the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We have not. The response should say so expressly, so that silence cannot later be argued as acceptance.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is our *conditional fallback*, which needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. None has been given. **Push back to 25%.** |
| **Thresholds (cl 12.2)** | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; excess only | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first dollar | The de minimis is 5x and the basket 5x ours. "Excess only" means the Seller never pays the first AUD 250k of valid claims. **Reject all three elements.** |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given. **Hold at 24 months.** |
| **"Limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)** | Default extends every limitation to every Claim | Separate Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories; no hidden general override | **This is a hidden general-regime override.** It would pull indemnities, covenant claims, payment obligations, tax and title into the general cap, basket and period, unless each is carved out word for word. **Delete it.** Reverse the default so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same caps and periods as general, "for administrative simplicity" | 100% cap; at least 6 years; outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Title is the core of a share purchase. A 20% cap on title means that if title fails we recover at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m price. **Reject outright.** |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | No fraud carve-out | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, as far as enforceable; non-waivable | **This is a critical point.** As drafted, it purports to cap and time-bar fraud claims and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. **Insert a full carve-out. This is not negotiable, and no one on our side can waive it.** |

### B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller generally discloses:

- the whole data room as at 22 Sept 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012);
- the Accounts and statutory registers;
- "publicly searchable corporate records."

This is the deemed-disclosure model our playbook rejects. Any fact buried anywhere in the data room or a public register would qualify every warranty.

Push back: only specific matters in the Disclosure Letter count, and only if fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the warranties. Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as disclosures. At most, they can be kept as a list of documents provided.

Paragraph 1.4 (no admission of breach or liability) is common and broadly acceptable. It must not, however, be read to qualify our right to require the consents and releases discussed below.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** This is extremely broad. It covers knowledge of the Buyer *or its advisers*, and "any matter discoverable from the data room or public records," which is constructive knowledge.

- **Delete it.**
- If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to *Seller* knowledge, held by named individuals, after reasonable enquiry.
- It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

Why this matters here: the Disclosure Letter itself tells us about Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006. Combined with cl 8.3 and general disclosure, the Seller could argue we have no claim for any of them. These matters therefore need conditions, completion mechanics and specific indemnities, not warranty protection alone.

### C. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

**Facts:**
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
- The change-control consent is in cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3.
- The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**

**Seller position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

**Problems:**
- A consent letter may itself be conditional, or may be ineffective if the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet. Delivery alone tells us nothing about whether the consent works.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size.

**Push back:**
- Make it a condition precedent that is satisfied only when (i) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent is delivered and (ii) evidence is provided that every cl 11.3 condition has been met before Completion.
- The Seller should commit to a stronger efforts standard, with an obligation to keep us informed and let us review the consent wording.
- We need a right not to complete if the condition fails, and no Seller right to waive it.

### D. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

**Facts:**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2.
- Not repaid; no discharge is in the data room (DL para 3).

**Seller position:** release "provided following Completion."

**Problems:**
- The change of control may itself trigger default or acceleration under cl 8.1.
- We would be paying the price while security remains over the Company's assets, and possibly over the shares.
- This is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis.

**Push back. We need all of the following at Completion:**
1. A current payout letter from Riverlark.
2. Direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow, treated as Debt deducted from the price.
3. Executed deeds of release and discharge of all security, including PPSR registrations, plus any share mortgage.

Any post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

### E. Employee bonuses (DD-005) and the funds flow

**Facts:**
- Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are conditional on Completion and continued employment.
- They are **not in the funds flow** (DL para 5).
- The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller." Yet the Company is the employer, so the obligation, and any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, would sit in the target after Completion.
- The Disclosure Letter does not say whether on-costs apply.

**Push back:** the AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs must be either:
- a specific line item treated as Debt or a transaction expense; or
- funded by the Seller,

backed by a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.

We should not accept a funds flow that silently leaves them out. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation. We should not assume a figure.

### F. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Facts:**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. The Seller itself notes this is not bank verification.
- There is no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** the indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate."

**Problem:** it covers only the payment, not the real risk. That risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials, together with any related infringement claims, loss of use or remediation costs.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or be free to use, the Ironquay Project Materials, including third-party claims.
- Keep this outside the general cap and basket.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** before Completion, the Seller pays all outstanding SOW3 fees and procures a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.

Do not treat AUD 180k as confirmed in either direction. Request bank evidence or an Ironquay statement of account.

### G. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

**Facts:**
- A download link went to an unintended external address.
- About 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary (DL para 6).

**Seller position:** "preliminary… not expected to be material."

The Seller's own disclosure does not support a materiality conclusion. Equally, we should **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any loss figure.

**Push back. Require:**
- preservation of all relevant logs and evidence;
- completion of a proper investigation, including whether the file was accessed;
- a documented assessment of any Notifiable Data Breaches obligation;
- regular updates to us, with our right to review findings before Completion.

Any risk allocation (for example a specific indemnity) should be framed by reference to the outcome. We should not put a number on it or concede immateriality.

### H. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

**Facts:** three related AUD 110k renewals (DD-008, DD-011). The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but its own Disclosure Letter says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Approach:** **assess, do not assume.** Request:
- the contracts;
- the renewal dates relative to Completion;
- termination rights;
- whether the three are linked or split, given the instruction to read them together;
- whether any amount is prepaid or accrued.

Do not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Do make sure the ordinary-course and leakage covenants would catch any renewal entered into outside the normal course before Completion.

### I. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **They are not.** Under our playbook they remain OPEN, with separate categories. We should not let them default into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime, which is another reason to delete the cl 12.3 "all Claims" override. For planning, assume no unlimited liability has been agreed and nothing has been resolved.

### J. Title (DD-012)

The Seller relies on the internal share register. That is a supplied source. The Seller's own para 10 concedes it is not verification by us.

**Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority:**
- a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
- original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
- PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, and evidence that no security exists over the shares (relevant given Riverlark);
- Seller board approvals and authority to sign;
- signed share transfer forms;
- confirmation of no options or convertible rights.

### K. Lower-priority items (not in our playbook)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the obligation appears to be notification only. Confirm the clause, and make the notice a completion deliverable or post-completion covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the restriction is on assignment, which a share sale may not trigger. Ask counsel to confirm there is no change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the contract.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / [STANDARD] / already accepted" framing in writing.** State that no fallback has been authorised. Check any claimed principal-level agreement directly with Amelia Frost.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; recovery from the first dollar.
4. **General claims period:** 24 months. 18 months is not available without written approval.
5. **Delete the cl 12.3 "applies to all Claims" override.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories separate.
6. **Fundamental/Title:** 100% cap; at least 6 years; outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
7. **Fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). Not negotiable.
8. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only; strike DL paras 1.1 and 1.2 as disclosures.
9. **Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.** At most, allow a named-person Seller knowledge qualifier with reasonable enquiry. It must never affect title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** condition precedent requiring an effective consent *plus* evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not satisfied merely on delivery; stronger efforts standard; no Seller waiver.
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and all releases (including PPSR) at Completion.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with a specific indemnity. Confirm the on-costs.
13. **Ironquay:** a broader IP indemnity outside general limits; keep the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment); verify the AUD 180k independently.
14. **DD-006:** preserve logs, complete the investigation and NDB assessment, provide regular updates. No materiality concession and no assumed breach or figure.
15. **Sandbar:** diligence requests, plus ordinary-course and leakage protection. No automatic Debt treatment.
16. **Tax/IP:** mark as OPEN in the mark-up; do not accept the general regime.
17. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence; DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Suggested next steps:**
- Prepare the mark-up and an issues list on this basis.
- Send the Seller a diligence request list covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus on-costs, Sandbar, DD-006 and title.
- Brief Amelia Frost on the Seller's claim of a principal-level settlement before responding.

- We need a right not to complete if the condition fails, and no Seller right to waive it.

### D. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

**Facts:**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2.
- Not repaid; no discharge is in the data room (DL para 3).

**Seller position:** release "provided following Completion."

**Problems:**
- The change of control may itself trigger default or acceleration under cl 8.1.
- We would be paying the price while security remains over the Company's assets, and possibly over the shares.
- This is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis.

**Push back. We need all of the following at Completion:**
1. A current payout letter from Riverlark.
2. Direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow, treated as Debt deducted from the price.
3. Executed deeds of release and discharge of all security, including PPSR registrations, plus any share mortgage.

Any post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

### E. Employee bonuses (DD-005) and the funds flow

**Facts:**
- Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are conditional on Completion and continued employment.
- They are **not in the funds flow** (DL para 5).
- The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller." Yet the Company is the employer, so the obligation, and any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, would sit in the target after Completion.
- The Disclosure Letter does not say whether on-costs apply.

**Push back:** the AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs must be either:
- a specific line item treated as Debt or a transaction expense; or
- funded by the Seller,

backed by a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.

We should not accept a funds flow that silently leaves them out. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation. We should not assume a figure.

### F. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Facts:**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. The Seller itself notes this is not bank verification.
- There is no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** the indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate."

**Problem:** it covers only the payment, not the real risk. That risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials, together with any related infringement claims, loss of use or remediation costs.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or be free to use, the Ironquay Project Materials, including third-party claims.
- Keep this outside the general cap and basket.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** before Completion, the Seller pays all outstanding SOW3 fees and procures a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.

Do not treat AUD 180k as confirmed in either direction. Request bank evidence or an Ironquay statement of account.

### G. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

**Facts:**
- A download link went to an unintended external address.
- About 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary (DL para 6).

**Seller position:** "preliminary… not expected to be material."

The Seller's own disclosure does not support a materiality conclusion. Equally, we should **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any loss figure.

**Push back. Require:**
- preservation of all relevant logs and evidence;
- completion of a proper investigation, including whether the file was accessed;
- a documented assessment of any Notifiable Data Breaches obligation;
- regular updates to us, with our right to review findings before Completion.

Any risk allocation (for example a specific indemnity) should be framed by reference to the outcome. We should not put a number on it or concede immateriality.

### H. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

**Facts:** three related AUD 110k renewals (DD-008, DD-011). The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but its own Disclosure Letter says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Approach:** **assess, do not assume.** Request:
- the contracts;
- the renewal dates relative to Completion;
- termination rights;
- whether the three are linked or split, given the instruction to read them together;
- whether any amount is prepaid or accrued.

Do not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Do make sure the ordinary-course and leakage covenants would catch any renewal entered into outside the normal course before Completion.

### I. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **They are not.** Under our playbook they remain OPEN, with separate categories. We should not let them default into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime, which is another reason to delete the cl 12.3 "all Claims" override. For planning, assume no unlimited liability has been agreed and nothing has been resolved.

### J. Title (DD-012)

The Seller relies on the internal share register. That is a supplied source. The Seller's own para 10 concedes it is not verification by us.

**Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority:**
- a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
- original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
- PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, and evidence that no security exists over the shares (relevant given Riverlark);
- Seller board approvals and authority to sign;
- signed share transfer forms;
- confirmation of no options or convertible rights.

### K. Lower-priority items (not in our playbook)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the obligation appears to be notification only. Confirm the clause, and make the notice a completion deliverable or post-completion covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the restriction is on assignment, which a share sale may not trigger. Ask counsel to confirm there is no change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the contract.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / [STANDARD] / already accepted" framing in writing.** State that no fallback has been authorised. Check any claimed principal-level agreement directly with Amelia Frost.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; recovery from the first dollar.
4. **General claims period:** 24 months. 18 months is not available without written approval.
5. **Delete the cl 12.3 "applies to all Claims" override.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories separate.
6. **Fundamental/Title:** 100% cap; at least 6 years; outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
7. **Fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). Not negotiable.
8. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only; strike DL paras 1.1 and 1.2 as disclosures.
9. **Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.** At most, allow a named-person Seller knowledge qualifier with reasonable enquiry. It must never affect title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** condition precedent requiring an effective consent *plus* evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not satisfied merely on delivery; stronger efforts standard; no Seller waiver.
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and all releases (including PPSR) at Completion.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with a specific indemnity. Confirm the on-costs.
13. **Ironquay:** a broader IP indemnity outside general limits; keep the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment); verify the AUD 180k independently.
14. **DD-006:** preserve logs, complete the investigation and NDB assessment, provide regular updates. No materiality concession and no assumed breach or figure.
15. **Sandbar:** diligence requests, plus ordinary-course and leakage protection. No automatic Debt treatment.
16. **Tax/IP:** mark as OPEN in the mark-up; do not accept the general regime.
17. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence; DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Suggested next steps:**
- Prepare the mark-up and an issues list on this basis.
- Send the Seller a diligence request list covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus on-costs, Sandbar, DD-006 and title.
- Brief Amelia Frost on the Seller's claim of a principal-level settlement before responding.
